sepsis.who.unknown: Community-acquired sepsis of unknown source: cefotaxime or ceftriaxone combined with amikacin or gentamicin; 7 days. Once the source is found, follow the infection-specific guidance.
sepsis.ssc.time_shock: Septic shock: give antimicrobials immediately, ideally within 1 hour of recognition.
sepsis.ssc.time_no_shock: No shock: investigate rapidly; if concern for infection persists, give antimicrobials within 3 hours.
sepsis.who.shock_dose: Dose adjustments may be required in septic shock; listed doses are for normal renal and hepatic function.
sepsis.ssc.mrsa: High MRSA risk: empiric MRSA coverage is recommended. The source table names no agent in this row; adding one is an expert decision.
sepsis.ssc.mdr: High risk of resistant organisms: two agents with Gram-negative coverage are suggested (this regimen already has two). Amikacin remains active against many ESBL producers.
sepsis.note.icu: Guidelines give no separate intensive care regimen; the table covers community-acquired sepsis. Hospital-acquired sepsis needs local resistance data and expert advice.
